mesoscaleDiscussions.areas: Southeast Nebraska into northeast Kansas...northwest Missouri...and southwest Iowa
mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A localized corridor of severe hail and wind potential may emerge over the next few hours across southeast Nebraska, northeast Kansas, and into adjacent portions of northwest Missouri and southwest Iowa. However, this threat will likely remain sufficiently isolated to preclude watch issuance.

details.label: Areas affected
details.text: Southeast Nebraska into northeast Kansas...northwest Missouri...and southwest Iowa

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Convective trends have been monitored over the past hour as an isolated thunderstorm developed across far southeast NE and crossed the MO River. More recently, additional attempts at deep convection are noted in radar and GOES IR imagery, and appear to be driven by strengthening isentropic ascent across a warm frontal zone as the nocturnal jet begins to slowly intensify (0-2 km winds have been increasing to 30-40 knots in upstream VWPs over the past 30-45 minutes). Despite a somewhat focused zone for initiation, the placement of this zone within the upper-level ridge axis suggests synoptic-scale forcing for ascent and deep-layer wind shear is limited for storm maintenance and/or intensification. The relatively short lifespan and recent demise of the initial cell crossing the MO River reflects these mitigating factors, despite an otherwise highly favorable thermodynamic environment (MUCAPE analyzed upwards of 4000-5000 J/kg). Over the next few hours, the expectation is for additional development of isolated cells and perhaps a few clusters to the north of the surface warm front. Very strong instability will favor robust updraft development that may pose a threat for isolated large hail and perhaps strong to severe downbursts. However, given the buoyancy-driven nature of this convection within a modestly sheared environment, storm organization and longevity may be limited. Furthermore, this activity should primarily reside within an MUCIN minimum co-located with the strongest isentropic ascent. Storm maintenance out of this corridor seems unlikely, and should spatially confine the severe threat. Given these limitations, watch issuance is not anticipated.

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Damaging wind potential continues within WW548.

details.label: Discussion
details.text: The line of thunderstorms across northern OH has weakened over the last hour. Instability decreases across eastern OH into far western PA. Further weakening is anticipated as the storms move toward this less favorable air mass. Damaging wind potential continues across the far northern portion of the line and with some redevelopment along the outflow across the southern portion of the line. A more favorably unstable air mass remains ahead of the new development near the southern portion of the line, though deep layer shear decreases with southward extent. Overall, damaging wind potential is expected to continue over the next couple of hours before gradual weakening occurs. A downstream watch is not currently anticipated but trends will be monitored.

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Supercells are likely to develop across eastern Iowa into northern Illinois this evening. Primary threat will be for large hail and damaging wind.

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A southwesterly low-level jet (LLJ) around 30-35 kts will move into portions of northern Illinois this evening. A surface boundary extends across northern Illinois. Near the boundary and the nose of the LLJ, there is good run to run agreement in CAM guidance that storms will develop across some portion of far eastern Iowa into northern Illinois within the warm advection regime this evening. Some radar returns and cloud cooling have been noted in the last 30 minutes across this area. The environment across this region is strongly unstable, with MLCAPE around 2000-4000 J/kg sampled by 00z RAOBs from DVN and ILX. Deep layer shear around 35-40 kts will increase with the LLJ later this evening. This regime will support supercells with the primary threat of large hail and damaging wind. For any supercell that can remain rooted in the surface, a tornado will be possible. A watch will likely be needed to cover this potential in the next couple of hours.

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The potential for severe winds will continue for the next 2-3 hours across much of WW 549 in western Nebraska. However, the most likely corridor for severe winds may emerge from the southern Nebraska Panhandle into far northeast Colorado and far southwest Nebraska.

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent echo top trends show deepening convective towers as a broken band of convection continues to push east into a reservoir of increasing MLCAPE. Downstream from this activity, the recent 00 UTC LBF sounding sampled very steep (8.7 C/km) mid-level lapse rates that are conducive for robust updrafts. However, warm temperatures between 850-700 mb are also yielding MLCIN on the order of -300 to -350 J/kg. Mixed-layer LFCs were estimated to be around 4 km, suggesting that a substantially deep cold pool will likely be needed to continue lifting parcels through the stable layer and maintain intensity of the line. Based on regional velocity/reflectivity data, it appears that such a cold pool is in the process of being established, but may not yet be sufficiently deep to maintain all portions of the line. Based on recent mesoanalysis estimates, MLCIN increases with eastward extent into central NE, but remains somewhat more modest across southwest NE, suggesting that the southern flank of the line may be favored for maintenance and/or further intensification over the next few hours. Given that this band has already produced measured gusts on the order of 55-65 mph, similar wind speeds appear possible for the short term (next hour or so), and may persist for the next few hours across southwest NE and far northeast CO.
